samples.summary: Escaping now depends on StarRocks honouring MySQL backslash escapes; under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES semantics `mysql.escape` output is injectable where the old quote-doubling was not
samples.evidence: `sql()` was changed from `'${value.replace(/'/g, "''")}'` to `mysql.escape(value)` (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:42-44). `mysql.escape` emits backslash escapes (`d'1\\` -> `'d\'1\\\\'`). That is only safe if the server treats `\` as an escape character inside string literals. StarRocks is MySQL-*protocol* compatible but its literal handling is not guaranteed to match, and MySQL itself under `NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES` treats `\` literally — in that mode `'a\'` produced by the escaper terminates the literal early and the remainder of the value lands in SQL as code, i.e. an injection the previous `''`-doubling (valid in BOTH modes) did not have. The result is interpolated verbatim into `document_id = ${id}` (line 98) and `document_id IN (${ids})` (line 161) with no prepared statement. Practical reachability is low today: the only values reaching `sql()` are server-generated document UUIDs (prisma schema.prisma:42 `@default(uuid())`, controller 404s on unknown ids) and `day()`-formatted dates, so I could not complete an attacker-controlled chain — hence low confidence, but the impact if a non-UUID id ever reaches the builder (e.g. an imported/legacy id) is warehouse SQL injection. Safest form is to keep it dialect-agnostic: reject any id not matching `^[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}$` before interpolation, or double quotes AND strip/escape backslashes.

samples.summary: No shape validation on the ids that are string-interpolated into warehouse SQL — the builders are the last line of defence and trust their caller entirely
samples.evidence: `buildQueries(documentId)` and `buildWorkspaceQueries(documentIds)` are public methods that interpolate their arguments straight into SQL (lines 98, 161) with escaping as the only defence, on an engine with no prepared statements. Nothing asserts the ids are UUID-shaped. Today the only caller passes a route param that must resolve in Postgres (analytics.controller.ts:163-166) and ids read from Postgres (line 225-228), so I could not reach it with hostile input — searched every call site (grep `buildQueries|buildWorkspaceQueries|getDocumentAnalytics|getWorkspaceAnalytics` across packages/backend/src: only analytics.controller.ts:177,231 and the specs). A cheap `/^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/i` guard (or throwing on any id containing a quote/backslash) would make the escaper's dialect assumptions irrelevant.
searchedFor: grep prisma.document.create / createDocument( to confirm ids are server-generated

samples.summary: Rows for documents missing from Postgres fall back to exposing the raw documentId as the title and are marked manageable for owners
samples.evidence: `title: d?.title ?? r.documentId` and `canManage: isDocumentManager(member.role, d?.authorID ?? null, userId)` (analytics.controller.ts:244-249). When the warehouse returns an id no longer present in `meta` the row surfaces a bare document id to the member and, for an `owner`, is marked `canManage: true` (author fallback `null` still passes on role). Not exploitable — the IN-list is built from the workspace's own docs (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:161) so the row can only be a doc deleted mid-request, and the detail endpoint 404s on it — but it is a fail-open default in an otherwise fail-closed annotation (contrast the warehouse's `canManage: false` placeholder at analytics-warehouse.service.ts:240).

verdict.reason: The `mysql.escape` interpolation exists as quoted (analytics-warehouse.service.ts:42-44, 98, 161), but no attacker-controlled string can reach `sql()`. The only production callers are analytics.controller.ts:177 and :231. The document endpoint resolves the `:id` param through `prisma.document.findUnique` and throws NotFoundException on any unknown value (analytics.controller.ts:163-166), so only ids that exist as rows proceed; those ids are always server-generated (`id String @default(uuid())`, prisma/schema.prisma:42) and no creation path accepts a client-supplied id (document.controller.ts:132-140, :214-222, api/v1/documents.controller.ts:54-65, api/v1/files.controller.ts:111-120 all omit `id`). The workspace endpoint sources ids exclusively from Postgres (analytics.controller.ts:225-232). The only other `sql()` inputs are `day()` outputs (`toISOString().slice(0,10)`, service line 45-47) with `resolveWindow` rejecting unparsable dates (controller 44-52), so `'`/`\` can never appear. Additionally the finding's premise is inverted: the prior `''`-doubling was NOT safe in both modes — under default MySQL/StarRocks semantics where backslash is an escape character, `a\'` breaks out of a quote-doubled literal, so the `mysql.escape` swap is a net hardening, not a regression. Adding an explicit UUID regex is a defense-in-depth suggestion, not a blocking injection.
